A federal judge, Mark Pittman, has ordered the disclosure of any agreements that may have led to a Musk-owned company withdrawing its antitrust allegations against Apple. Details below.

Judge orders disclosure of any settlement reached with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a voluntary motion with the court to dismiss their allegations against Apple, with the withdrawal being a final decision. The lawsuit was filed by the two companies last year against Apple and OpenAI.

According to the initial complaint, Apple and OpenAI were accused of colluding via an agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence, thereby preventing competing AI applications from gaining exposure on the App Store. Both Apple and OpenAI have denied the allegations.

In court documents filed earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI only stated that they "had reached a settlement of the claims against Apple in this case," while emphasising that they did not intend to withdraw the allegations against OpenAI.

According to POLITICO, which first reported the news, the presiding judge, Mark Pittman, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit to the court "any agreement or series of agreements reached with Apple to resolve the plaintiffs' claims against Apple in this case."

This ruling was made in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI, which sought to compel X and SpaceXAI to disclose the agreements they had reached with Apple to settle the dispute. Pittman also ordered the companies concerned to respond to OpenAI's motion by noon on 17 September.
